requirements.evidence: All contract items present: entities migration with `unique('entities_slug_unique')` and softDeletes (2026_10_29_065751_create_entities_table.php:17-19); entity_memberships with cascading FKs, `role` default 'employee', `storedAs("case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end")` owner_seq and both named unique indexes (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-31); Entity getRouteKeyName/memberships/users/owner (app/Models/Entity.php:49-79); EntityMembership cast + scopes + relations; UserRole with manageable(); User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (app/Models/User.php:177-200); factories with owner/admin/employee states; both policies implement the exact rules (owner-membership delete denied first, then self-removal, then manager check — EntityMembershipPolicy.php:263-274). docs/database-schema.md drops owner_membership_id as required.

conventions.evidence: Policies in app/Policies, mass assignment set deliberately via `#[Fillable([...])]` matching User.php style, reversible down() in both migrations, migration filenames look generator-produced, CHANGELOG under Unreleased and database-schema.md/docs/README.md updated. Minor: docs/database-schema.md Modeling Notes describe unimplemented behavior (ownership transfer 'in the same transaction', owner may remove themselves 'after transferring ownership') as if it existed.

security.evidence: Every ability is deny-by-default for non-members (membershipFor returns null -> false); owner membership can never be deleted (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:265); manageSettings owner-only (EntityPolicy.php:342); enum compared strictly with `in_array(..., true)`. Limited gap: assignRole lets an admin target the owner's own membership (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:255-258), so a future action relying solely on this policy could let an admin demote the owner; the task wording permits it, but it is worth a guard or note.

tests.evidence: Pest feature tests cover schema columns/index names, factory defaults and states, DB default role, enum cast and manageable(), scopes, owner_seq generation, second-owner rejection vs. different entities each with an owner, any number of non-owners, duplicate member rejection, cascades, soft delete/route key, owner() null case, membershipFor null, and every policy ability with owner/admin/employee/outsider/other-entity-member cases plus no-arg construction (tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php, EntityMembershipPolicyTest.php).

simplicity.evidence: Lean models and policies reusing Laravel features (generated column, hasOne with where, policy auto-discovery). Small duplication: `isManager` is implemented twice (EntityPolicy.php:356-363 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:279-286), and EntityPolicy::membershipFor (EntityPolicy.php:348-351) is a trivial wrapper around User::membershipFor. Explicit `$table->index('user_id')` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:532) is mostly redundant with the FK index.

readability.evidence: Short, well-named methods with PHPDoc, consistent with sibling User.php style; helpful comment explaining the owner_seq trick (create_entity_memberships_table.php:22-23); tests are descriptive. No dead code or debug output; one unused `$membership` variable in EntityModelTest 'users relation exposes the membership role' test is trivial.

scope.evidence: No routes, pages, session or middleware were added; every code file serves the task. Docs go slightly beyond what was implemented (speculative ownership-transfer notes in database-schema.md), and an existing CHANGELOG 'Changed' line was edited to remove the circular-FK mention, which is justifiable given the task.

issues.explanation: assignRole allows an admin to act on the owner's membership, so a future role-assignment action relying only on this policy could let an admin demote the owner; consider denying when the target is the owner membership.
Docs describe ownership transfer 'in the same transaction' and owner self-removal after transfer, behavior that this change does not implement.
The owner/admin check is duplicated across both policies, and EntityPolicy::membershipFor is a one-line wrapper over User::membershipFor.
Explicit index on user_id duplicates the index the foreign key already creates on MariaDB.

issues.location: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php ('the users relation exposes the membership role on the pivot')

review.summary: The change adds the entities and entity_memberships migrations (including the portable owner_seq generated column with its unique index), the Entity/EntityMembership models, the UserRole enum, User relations, factories, both policies and the documentation updates, all backed by thorough Pest tests covering the database constraints and every authorization path. It meets the contract fully. Only small issues remain: some duplicated policy helpers, docs that describe ownership-transfer behavior that isn't implemented yet, and assignRole allowing admins to target the owner membership. I would approve it with nits.
